component.name: USB Guard
component.summary: Review and control which USB devices may connect

description.p: A COSMIC desktop front-end for USBGuard, with a system-tray status icon. Plug in a device and you are asked about it, with enough information to answer. Every decision is recorded, and you can change your mind later.

ul.li: Prompts when a new device is connected, showing its name, IDs, serial number, port and interface classes
Warns about devices that present a keyboard interface and could inject keystrokes
Lists every device USBGuard can see, with internal hubs filtered out by default
Lists devices that are not plugged in but still have a standing rule, so a decision can be changed without them
Revoke removes a device's standing rule and blocks it in one step
Optionally runs a program of your choosing when a specific trusted device is connected and authorised
Notifies when a standing rule refuses a device without asking, so it does not just silently fail to work
Shows a status icon in the system tray and can start with your session
Keeps a searchable history of every device event and decision
Checks that USBGuard is genuinely protecting the system, not merely installed, and gives you the command to fix each problem

description.p: This application enforces nothing itself. USBGuard does. It requires the usbguard daemon and its D-Bus interface to be installed and running.
